questions.q: Why is each cleaning decision written as its own small function chained with .pipe()?
options: Because pandas requires it
Each step is readable, reusable, and can be tested on its own
It makes the data larger
It removes the need for a raw data file
questions.explain: Small single-purpose functions are easy to read and test, and .pipe() lets you chain them in the order of your cleaning plan.

questions.q: How does the capstone handle a column holding dates in two formats (like 2024-05-03 and 11/23/2024)?
options: Parse with each format using errors="coerce", then fill the gaps of one result with the other
Delete every row that uses the US format
Convert dates to plain text
Sort the column alphabetically
questions.explain: Each pattern parses only the rows that match it and returns NaT for the rest; fillna combines the two results into one datetime column.

questions.q: The cleaning funnel went 1,530 raw rows, 1,500 after dedupe, 1,442 after the quantity rule. Why report these numbers?
options: They prove the code has no bugs
Because pandas prints them automatically
Readers can see how much data your cleaning removed and judge whether it could bias the results
They are needed to draw the chart
questions.explain: Row counts through the cleaning steps make your work auditable and reveal whether a rule discards a meaningful share of the data.

questions.q: In our illustrative data, average quantity per order is about 3 in every discount band, while return rates rise with the discount. What is the most careful conclusion?
options: Discounts cause returns and should be banned
Discounts definitely double sales
There is no relationship of any kind
Discounts did not raise items per order, and higher returns in discounted bands are an association worth investigating, not proof of cause
questions.explain: The data shows an association, and the deepest band has only 103 orders. Claims of causation need stronger evidence, such as the statistical methods in the next course.

questions.q: Why is the revenue calculation restricted to orders with status "complete"?
options: Returned and cancelled orders do not produce revenue for the shop
Because complete orders are the only ones with prices
Because pandas cannot group other statuses
To make the chart look better
questions.explain: We defined revenue up front as quantity x price x (1 - discount) on completed orders only. Returns and cancellations aren't kept revenue.
